key_insight: The study introduces the Neurocognitive Speech Taxonomy (NST), an interpretable framework that maps 314 voice features into 7 neurocognitive domains to help explain voice-based biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease.
clinical_relevance: NST may improve interpretability and fairness of AI voice screening tools for cognitive impairment, potentially aiding earlier detection and monitoring of Alzheimer’s-related change.
method: Mapped 314 speech/voice features to 7 neurocognitive domains.
Validated NST across 3 cohorts (total N=1,479) with demographic, neuropsychological, biomarker, and imaging data.
Tested stability, diagnostic discrimination, longitudinal tracking, and equity versus standard cognitive testing.
evidence_signal: NST showed stable cross-cohort structure (Mantel r = 0.71–0.77), differentiated MCI and AD biomarker status, tracked cognitive change, and correlated with hippocampal volume (up to r = 0.28).
watch_item: Findings support interpretability and validity, but the framework still needs broader external validation before routine clinical implementation.
paper_title: A neurocognitive speech taxonomy for voice biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease
